children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18 and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! To help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to know a bit more about his current situation.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training? (For example, is he in sixth form, college, doing A-levels, or any other approved course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! Since Alex is 18 and in approved education, that's a good start.

Now I need to check a few more things. Is Alex working at all? And if so, how many hours per week does he work?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working. He's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, that's helpful to know. Just a couple more questions:

Do you live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. But no, Alex doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand your arrangement a bit better.

Do you contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep - for example, by providing money for food, clothes, pocket money, or contributing to his accommodation costs? And if so, roughly how much do you contribute per week or per month?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help with things like clothes, food, and his other expenses. I give him about £30 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know you're contributing £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep.

Just to clarify - where is Alex currently living? Is he living with another parent, a relative, at university accommodation, or somewhere else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living with his mum, my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is an important question:

Is Alex's mum currently claiming Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ **Age and Education**: Alex is 18 and studying for his A-levels at sixth form college, which counts as approved education. You can claim Child Benefit for children under 20 who are in approved education or training.

✓ **Financial Contribution**: Even though Alex lives with his mum, you're contributing £30 per week towards his upkeep (clothes, food, and expenses). This is more than the current Child Benefit rate of £25.60 per week for one child, which means you meet the requirement for claiming while he lives elsewhere.

✓ **No Competing Claim**: Alex's mum is not claiming Child Benefit for him, so there's no conflict.

✓ **No Disqualifying Work**: Alex isn't working 24 hours or more per week.

**Important note**: If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might need to pay some or all of it back through your tax return.

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit for Alex!

Although Alex doesn't live with you (he lives with his mum), you are contributing £30 per week towards his upkeep. According to the rules, you can continue to get Child Benefit for a child who lives with someone else if you contribute to their upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment. The current Child Benefit rate for one child is £25.60 per week, and your contribution of £30 per week exceeds this amount. Upkeep includes clothes, food, and other expenses, which matches what you're providing. Additionally, Alex's mum is not claiming Child Benefit for him, so there is no conflict with another claim. Alex is not working 24 hours or more per week, and you live in the UK. Therefore, you meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit for Alex.
